record.original_question: In Euclidean 3-space E^3, are the only finite type surfaces minimal surfaces together with open portions of spheres and circular cylinders?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.A. The only surfaces of finite type in E^3 are minimal surfaces, and open portions of spheres and circular cylinders.
The immersion x is said to be of finite type if the position vector field of M in E^m, also denoted by x, can be expressed as a finite sum of E^m-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $x : M \to \mathbb{E}^3$ be an isometric immersion of a connected surface $M$ into Euclidean 3-space, with induced Laplace–Beltrami operator $\Delta$. The immersion $x$ (equivalently, the surface $M$) is said to be of finite type if the position vector field $x$ can be written as a finite sum
$$x = x_0 + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $x_0 \in \mathbb{E}^3$ is constant and $x_1, \ldots, x_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^3$-valued smooth maps on $M$ satisfying $\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i$ for real numbers $\lambda_i$. A surface in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is called minimal if its mean curvature vanishes identically.

Prove or disprove: the only surfaces of finite type in $\mathbb{E}^3$ are minimal surfaces, open portions of round spheres, and open portions of circular cylinders.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open in general. The literature confirms that, to date, the only known finite-type surfaces in Euclidean 3-space are minimal surfaces, open pieces of spheres, and open pieces of circular cylinders, and partial results have established the classification under additional hypotheses (e.g., for tubes, quadrics, surfaces of revolution, spiral surfaces, or under conditions like $\Delta H = AH$), but no full proof or counterexample is known.

status_evidence.title: On Surfaces of finite Chen-type
status_evidence.snippet: Up to this moment the only known finite Chen-type surfaces in E^3 are portions of spheres, circular cylinders and minimal surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: As of recent literature the conjecture is unresolved and only the listed examples are known.

status_evidence.title: On surfaces of finite type in Euclidean 3-space
status_evidence.snippet: Surfaces of E^3 satisfying ΔH = AH are either minimal, or an open piece of a sphere, or of a right circular cylinder.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results support the conjecture under additional hypotheses.
